clue.text: Formal shirt front inclined mostly to contain stay

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped
to contain asks the shortened word to hold another word inside it

blocks.note: prone means inclined or disposed to
to last is to stay or endure

explanation.surface: Someone describes a dress shirt whose front leans over a supporting stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' suggests the stiffening in a shirt collar, which suits the surface; here it is a verb meaning endure.
explanation.definitionFit: A plastron is the stiffened, starched panel on the breast of a formal dress shirt.

clue.text: It may be doled out in pay — in Rangoon

definitions.text: It may be doled out in pay — in Rangoon

indicators.note: doled out means handed round and spread about, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A small coin is handed out as wages in Burma's old capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: Rangoon (now Yangon) is in Burma, whose currency includes this coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A pya is a small Burmese coin, a hundredth of a kyat, so it is money that might be paid out in Rangoon.

clue.text: Sort of extension, part of Hawaiian alteration going up

indicators.note: part of says the letters lie inside the words that follow
in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A builder discusses a type of house extension, part of a Hawaiian renovation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hawaiian setting fits the answer, which is a Hawaiian word.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanai is a veranda or roofed patio, a kind of open-sided extension to a house, originally in Hawaii.

clue.text: Local US cop, bent one accepting crooked treat? (12, two words)

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of true, so these letters are twisted into a new order
accepting means taking in, so the first word receives the other inside it

blocks.note: a stooper is one who bends or stoops
the letters of treat, rearranged

explanation.surface: An American policeman who is corrupt takes a dodgy backhander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' wants to mean corrupt, as British slang does for a crooked policeman; here it means stooping.
explanation.definitionFit: A state trooper is a member of a US state police force, so a regional American police officer.

clue.text: Bones I gnawed up with extremes of avarice

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the preceding letters are read from bottom to top
extremes of keeps only the first and last letters of the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
bit is the past tense of bite, to gnaw
the first and last letters of avarice

explanation.surface: A greedy dog confesses to chewing bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibiae is the Latin plural of tibia, the shinbone, so the word names a set of bones.

clue.text: Copper turned up in swoop (at dawn?) unusually hoarse

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the letters are flipped to read bottom to top
in places the flipped letters inside the following word

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a dawn raid is a sudden swoop, typically by police

explanation.surface: A policeman in a dawn raid shouts himself unusually hoarse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer, fitting the raid, but it is the metal. 'Unusually' belongs to the definition, flagging the rarity of this form.
explanation.definitionFit: Raucid is a rare variant of raucous, meaning harsh or hoarse in sound, hence an unusual word for hoarse.

clue.text: Like navvies at work high tension cut short?

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its final letter
high as in intoxicated, so the letters are in a disordered state

blocks.note: tension without its last letter

explanation.surface: Labourers at work under high-tension power lines, with the tension cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High tension' reads as electrical jargon; high is the anagram signal. A navvy is a British word for a manual labourer on building or roadworks.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers on a building job are physically present at the location, so on site describes navvies at their work.

clue.text: Opera star Rita, icon, unusually branching out

indicators.note: unusually means in an unaccustomed way, so the letters take an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: a diva is a celebrated female opera singer
the letters of Rita and icon, rearranged

explanation.surface: Rita, a soprano and an icon, is uncharacteristically trying something new.
explanation.definitionFit: Divarication is the act of spreading apart or forking, so it is a noun for branching out.

clue.text: Its target is flying in company as of old

blocks.note: first meaning: a surface-to-air missile, aimed at aircraft
second meaning: an obsolete word for together

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic description of a missile whose targets are things in flight; the second is an archaic adverb listed in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: SAM abbreviates surface-to-air missile, a weapon fired at aircraft; separately, sam is an old dialect word meaning together.

clue.text: Braid is shortened — not in fashion — pain

indicators.note: shortened means the word is contracted, losing letters as in an apostrophe form

blocks.note: is contracts to 's
out of fashion is simply out
an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: A dressmaker complains that braid trim is unfashionable and a pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Soutache is a narrow flat decorative braid used to trim garments, so it is a kind of braid.

clue.text: Epitome of wisdom getting two top marks in sequence?

blocks.note: A is the top mark; this is the first of the two
then means next in order, so it sits between the two marks
the second of the two top marks

explanation.surface: A wise student earns two straight A grades.
explanation.walkthrough: Two top marks in sequence reads literally as A then A.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena is the Greek goddess of wisdom, so she personifies it.

clue.text: More than one strong wine is spoiling, I'm sorry to say

blocks.note: mars means spoils or blights
alas is an expression of regret

explanation.surface: A regretful note that several strong wines have gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsala is a fortified wine from Sicily, so the plural names more than one such strong wine.

clue.text: Paraguayan tuber, I? I'll be cooked there with a burger pan

definitions.text: Paraguayan tuber, I? I'll be cooked there with a burger pan

indicators.note: cooked means prepared and changed, so the letters are worked into a different order

blocks.note: all these letters are the starting stock
these letters come out of the stock, leaving the answer

explanation.surface: A tuber from Paraguay speaks, wondering whether it will end up cooked alongside a burger in a pan.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: the answer plus A BURGER PAN shuffles to PARAGUAYAN TUBER I, so taking those letters away from the clue's first words leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The yautia is a starchy edible root grown in tropical America, and the whole clue describes it as a Paraguayan tuber headed for the pan.

clue.text: Regional flora and fauna displaying breadth a little bit

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for breadth
an iota is a tiny amount

explanation.surface: A naturalist notes that a region's wildlife shows only a small amount of variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Biota is the collective term for the plant and animal life of a particular area.

clue.text: Treatment for alcoholics? Answer includes prohibition, end of booze

indicators.note: includes means one part holds another inside it
end of picks out only the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: ANS is a common abbreviation for answer
tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, a ban
the final letter of the word booze

explanation.surface: A reply about curing drinkers that brings in a ban and the end of drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation is split by the ban: its last letter falls after the inserted word. Tabu is a recognised spelling of taboo.
explanation.definitionFit: Antabuse is a trade name for disulfiram, a drug that makes drinking alcohol unpleasant and so is used to treat alcoholism.

clue.text: Joins in seat damaged after lorry's involved in offence

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so one word sits within another
something damaged is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged
after places the rearranged seat at the end, following the other part

blocks.note: to take the pip is to take offence; pip here means annoyance or umbrage
an artic is an articulated lorry, a large truck with a separate cab
the four letters of seat, reshuffled

explanation.surface: A court report of someone damaging a seat after their lorry was caught up in a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: An artic is the British word for an articulated lorry, a semitrailer truck; to take the pip is an old British idiom for taking offence.
explanation.definitionFit: To participate is to take part, and joins in is an idiomatic phrasal verb meaning exactly that.

clue.text: Pure plot ruined when restricted by local rate

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the word's letters are broken up and rearranged
restricted by means hemmed in, so the rearranged letters sit within another word

blocks.note: sess is a Scots and Irish word for a tax or rate
the letters of plot, rearranged

explanation.surface: A pristine garden plot is spoilt by the local council tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotless means free from any stain or blemish, so it is a synonym of pure.

clue.text: Incentivize ministry that is limiting tax

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing on both sides, so the tax is held inside

blocks.note: MoT stands for the Ministry of Transport
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A government department encourages people by capping a tax.
explanation.walkthrough: The MoT was Britain's Ministry of Transport, still known for the annual MOT test of vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: To motivate someone is to give them a reason or incentive to act, which is what incentivize means.

clue.text: Arched gateway in honour of Rajput prince

blocks.note: a toast or dedication is made to someone, in their honour
a rana is a Rajput prince in India

explanation.surface: An arch is put up as a memorial to an Indian prince.
explanation.definitionFit: A torana is the ornamental arched gateway at the entrance to a Buddhist or Hindu shrine.

clue.text: Pinto at Ayr. It's nobbled with dope

indicators.note: a nobbled racehorse has been tampered with, so these letters are interfered with and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written; the 's is read as has
taken as written

explanation.surface: A racing tip: a piebald horse running at Ayr racecourse has been drugged.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinto looks like a horse's name, but it is the definition: a pinto is a piebald horse, and 'at Ayr' (a Scottish town) flags a Scots word. To nobble a horse is to drug it to stop it winning.
explanation.definitionFit: Pioted is a Scots adjective for pied or piebald, which is what pinto means, describing a horse with patches of two colours.

clue.text: Abnormal appetite expands centre of belt on a large scale

indicators.note: centre of keeps only the middle letters of the following word
expands means one word pushes the other apart by sitting in its middle

blocks.note: the two middle letters of belt
pica is a craving to eat non-food substances such as earth or chalk

explanation.surface: A big appetite makes the middle of someone's belt stretch hugely.
explanation.definitionFit: Epical is a variant of epic, meaning grand or heroic in scale, so it fits on a large scale as an adjective.

clue.text: Dark blues coach dropping No. 4 pipped in race

indicators.note: dropping the fourth one means the letter in fourth place is removed

blocks.note: Oxford University sports teams wear dark blue, so they are the Dark Blues
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: The Oxford rowing coach, missing the fourth oarsman, was narrowly beaten in the Boat Race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dark Blues are Oxford, Cambridge being the Light Blues. TRAIN loses its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrun is to beat in a race, so outran is a past-tense synonym of pipped, meaning beaten narrowly.

clue.text: Pustules, inflamed, I got in centre of quat

indicators.note: centre of keeps only the middle letters of the word after it
got in means entered, so these words go inside the other part

blocks.note: the two middle letters of quat
inflamed skin is red
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with inflamed spots complains of getting one in the middle of a pimple.
explanation.walkthrough: Quat is Shakespeare's word for a pimple, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Uredia are the rust-coloured spore-producing pustules of rust fungi on plants; the singular is uredium.

clue.text: Hawkish US politician once galumphing forward

indicators.note: galumphing means moving clumsily, so the letters lurch into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
on means forward, as in move on

explanation.surface: A warlike American politician of old lumbering clumsily ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' seems to mean former; it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A neocon, short for neoconservative, is a US right-winger known for interventionist, hawkish foreign policy.

clue.text: Bones found in isolated spot near Naples

blocks.note: first meaning: the plural of ischium, the lower hip bone
second meaning: an island in the Bay of Naples

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests skeletal remains turned up on a remote site; 'isolated spot' is a playful way of saying island.
explanation.definitionFit: Ischia is both the plural of the pelvic bone ischium and the volcanic island in the Gulf of Naples.

clue.text: Wherein guilty one may be caught? He escapes untouched

indicators.note: escapes means gets out, so that word leaves the longer phrase

blocks.clueFragment: Wherein guilty one may be caught?
blocks.note: a culprit is caught in the act
taken as written

explanation.surface: A culprit who should have been caught red-handed gets away scot-free.
explanation.walkthrough: IN THE ACT loses HE to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Intact means unharmed or not damaged, so it fits untouched as an adjective.

clue.text: Old bar to avoid, stocking last of beer

indicators.note: stocking means holding in stock, so one word keeps a letter inside
last of keeps only the final letter of the next word

blocks.note: to spare something is to do without it or avoid it
the final letter of beer

explanation.surface: A pub that is best avoided, though it still stocks beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, as in the surface; it is a wooden rail. Sparre is a Spenserian spelling of spar.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparre is an archaic form of spar, a pole or bar, such as one used to bolt a door.

clue.text: Sugary stuff, i.e. sort like jelly?

indicators.note: jelly wobbles and loses its shape, so the letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of i.e. and sort together

explanation.surface: Someone explains that a sweet substance is the sort that sets like jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: A triose is a simple sugar molecule with three carbon atoms, so it is a sugary substance in the chemist's sense.

clue.text: Raw minced tuber

indicators.note: minced means chopped up finely, so the letters are cut up and reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe step: an uncooked potato, chopped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raw' and 'minced' both sound like kitchen words; raw is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Brute as an adjective means crude or unrefined, as in brute force or brute matter, the sense of raw.

clue.text: Agitated lot over to left of a Conservative 'putting clock back'?

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the following letters are thrown into a new order
to left of places the stirred-up part first, before the remaining words

blocks.note: the seven letters of lot over, rearranged
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A flustered crowd is set against a Tory who wants to turn the clock back.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: turning a clock back means turning its hands anticlockwise, which is the direction of rotation the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Levorotatory describes a substance that rotates polarised light to the left, that is anticlockwise, the way clock hands turn when put back.

clue.text: Flaky squad initially in need of drilling?

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: the opening letter of squad
carious means decayed, describing a tooth that needs a dentist's drill

explanation.surface: A sloppy military squad that badly needs drill practice.
explanation.walkthrough: Drilling suggests parade-ground drill for the squad; it is the dentist's drill, and the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarious is a botanical term for thin, dry and membranous, like a papery bract, so flaky is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Poet's declaimed without love poems coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from bottom to top, backwards
without means lacking, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: odes are lyric poems
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A poet recited verse that came up short on love.
explanation.walkthrough: Poet's flags a word found in poetry; here Spenser's spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sed is a Spenserian spelling of said, the past tense of say, meaning declaimed or spoke.

clue.text: I'll be fixed in place once positioned

indicators.note: be fixed in means placed firmly inside, so the single letter goes within the other word

blocks.note: the letter I, with 'll read as will
sted is an obsolete spelling of stead, meaning a place

explanation.surface: Someone declares they will stay put once they have been placed somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' looks like it belongs with positioned, but it marks the old word for place.
explanation.definitionFit: Sited is the past participle of to site, meaning located or placed in position.

clue.text: Thick bit of toast, cold, accompanying course

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a course is a route or way taken

explanation.surface: A chunk of cold toast is served alongside a meal course.
explanation.definitionFit: A croûte is a thick slice of fried or toasted bread used as a base for savoury food.

clue.text: Means of soliciting reply, very Scottish

blocks.note: first meaning: a stamped addressed envelope, sent so the recipient can respond
second meaning: the Scots form of so

explanation.walkthrough: An SAE is the stamped addressed envelope a British letter-writer encloses to get a reply.
explanation.definitionFit: The initialism names a return envelope, and the Scots word sae is their spelling of so, meaning very.

clue.text: Fiancée, 'idden, veiled, accepting X

indicators.note: veiled means disguised, so these letters appear in a changed form
accepting means taking in, so the disguised letters hold the number inside

blocks.note: hidden with its H dropped, as the apostrophe shows
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A bride-to-be, h-droppingly hidden behind her veil, accepts a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: X looks like a kiss on a love letter; it is the Roman ten, placed inside the rearranged IDDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: One's intended is an informal noun for the person one is engaged to marry, a fiancée or fiancé.
